claim_1.claim: ELISpot analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day -7, day 0, day 1, day 7, and day 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed influenza vaccine-specific IgG+ antibody secreting cells increased on day 7 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: As expected, we observed strong, but highly variable, increases in influenza vaccine-specific IgG+ antibody secreting cells on day 7 (Figure 3A).
Figure 3. Post-vaccination changes in serologic, cellular and transcriptomic parameters (A) Increased antigen-specific antibody secreting cells on day 7 following vaccination measured by ELISpot.

claim_2.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day -7, day 0, day 1, day 7, and day 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed largely non-overlapping gene-expression signatures on day 1 and day 7 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: As previously reported (Bucasas et al., 2011; Nakaya et al., 2011; Obermoser et al., 2013), we also found coherent changes in gene expression, with largely non-overlapping signatures on days 1 and 7 (Figures 3B and 3C).

Figure 3. Post-vaccination changes in serologic, cellular and transcriptomic parameters (B) Heatmap of genes from days -7, 1, 7 and 70 that changed significantly compared to day 0 (FDR<0.05 and absolute log-fold-change > 0.2; fold-change from day 0 is indicated by color). Genes with similar patterns of change were grouped by clustering analysis (indicated by the color bars on the left.) (C) Coherently changed genes in the clusters from B. Right: Representative immunological pathways enriched in coherently changing genes on days 1 and 7 (see Methods).

claim_3.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day -7, day 0, day 1, day 7, and day 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed innate immune-cell activation pathways, including Interferon-related genes, on day 1 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Overall, day 1 responses included pathways reflecting innate immune-cell activation, including Interferon-related genes, as observed by others (Bucasas et al., 2011; Nakaya et al., 2011; Obermoser et al., 2013) (Figure 3C and Table S3).

Figure 3. Post-vaccination changes in serologic, cellular and transcriptomic parameters (C) Coherently changed genes in the clusters from B. Right: Representative immunological pathways enriched in coherently changing genes on days 1 and 7 (see Methods).

claim_4.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day -7, day 0, day 1, day 7, and day 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed adaptive pathways, including Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) stress and N-glycan biosynthesis, were more predominant on day 7 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: By day 7, adaptive pathways were more predominant, including those strongly associated with plasmablasts, such as “Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) stress” and “N-glycan biosynthesis” (see below) (Gass et al., 2004; Iwakoshi et al., 2003).

claim_5.claim: flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day -7, day 0, day 1, day 7, and day 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed largely non-overlapping changes in cell-subset frequencies on day 1 and day 7 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: As with the transcriptome, changes in subset frequencies on days 1 and 7 were largely non-overlapping (Figure 3D).

Figure 3. Post-vaccination changes in serologic, cellular and transcriptomic parameters (D) Coherently-changed cell populations on days 1 and 7 post-vaccination (FDR<0.05 and >10% change from day 0). Blue and brown boxes denote populations considered “innate” and “adaptive”, respectively.

claim_6.claim: flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day -7, day 0, day 1, day 7, and day 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed CD40+ and CD86+ monocytes and IFNα+ plasmacytoid DCs changed on day 1 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Again, day 1 changes reflected activation of innate immune cells, including CD40+ and CD86+ monocytes (ID65 and ID67) and IFNa+ plasmacytoid DCs (ID78), populations that have been linked to vaccination efficacy and responses to influenza (Fonteneau et al., 2003; van Duin et al., 2007).

Figure 3. Post-vaccination changes in serologic, cellular and transcriptomic parameters (D) Coherently-changed cell populations on days 1 and 7 post-vaccination (FDR<0.05 and >10% change from day 0). Blue and brown boxes denote populations considered “innate” and “adaptive”, respectively.

claim_7.claim: flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day -7, day 0, day 1, day 7, and day 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed activation-associated CD8+ and CD4+ T-cell populations and both naïve and memory B-cell populations changed on day 1 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: However, we also observed changes in adaptive cell populations, particularly those reflecting activation of CD8+ and CD4+ T cells, as well as both naïve and memory B cells (Kaminski et al., 2012).

Figure 3. Post-vaccination changes in serologic, cellular and transcriptomic parameters (D) Coherently-changed cell populations on days 1 and 7 post-vaccination (FDR<0.05 and >10% change from day 0). Blue and brown boxes denote populations considered “innate” and “adaptive”, respectively.

claim_8.claim: flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day -7, day 0, day 1, day 7, and day 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed plasmablasts, a related CD20+CD27+CD38+ B-cell subset, and activated T-cell populations changed on day 7 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Day 7 responses primarily reflected changes in adaptive cell populations, including plasmablasts (ID87) as expected, but also a related CD20+ B subset that expressed CD27 and CD38 (ID96, Figure S3), as well as activated T cell populations.

Figure 3. Post-vaccination changes in serologic, cellular and transcriptomic parameters (D) Coherently-changed cell populations on days 1 and 7 post-vaccination (FDR<0.05 and >10% change from day 0). Blue and brown boxes denote populations considered “innate” and “adaptive”, respectively.

claim_9.claim: microneutralization assay analysis of serum from 63 healthy individuals at day 0 and day 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed day 70/day 0 fold-change in titer was positively associated with day 7 fold-change in titer and effector B-cell responses.

sources.quote: Since the day 70-day 0 fold-change in titer correlated with both the day 7 fold-change in titer and effector B cell responses, and thus reflected both short- and long-term responses (Figures S4B and S4C), we used day 70 titer responses as the endpoint for subsequent analyses.

claim_10.claim: microneutralization assay analysis of serum from 63 healthy individuals at day 0 and day 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed higher initial titers were negatively associated with day 70/day 0 fold-changes in titers.

sources.quote: Interestingly, subjects with higher initial titers tended to have lower fold-changes.

Figure 4. Post-vaccination responses depend on baseline serology and memory B-cell status (A) Relationship between initial and fold-change (day 70/day 0) in titer for A/Uruguay after vaccination (see Figure S4 for other viruses). Histogram at left shows distribution of the titer responses.

claim_11.claim: flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from the low-initial-titer group 1 (n=33) and high-initial-titer group 2 (n=26) at day 7 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed significantly greater increases in plasmablasts (ID87) in the more naïve group 1 compared to group 2.

sources.quote: However, the more naïve group exhibited significantly greater increases in plasmablasts (ID87) and seasonal vaccine-specific ELISpot responses on day 7 (Figure 4C).

Figure 4. Post-vaccination responses depend on baseline serology and memory B-cell status (B) Heatmap showing two distinct groups of subjects identified based on robust clustering analysis of day 0 serologic and memory B-cell variables (see Methods) (C) Post-vaccination changes in plasmablast frequencies on day 7 for the low (1) and high (2) initial titer groups from B.

claim_12.claim: ELISpot analysis of PBMCs from the low-initial-titer group 1 (n=33) and high-initial-titer group 2 (n=26) at day 7 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed significantly greater seasonal vaccine-specific IgG+ responses in the more naïve group 1 compared to group 2.

sources.quote: However, the more naïve group exhibited significantly greater increases in plasmablasts (ID87) and seasonal vaccine-specific ELISpot responses on day 7 (Figure 4C).

Figure 4. Post-vaccination responses depend on baseline serology and memory B-cell status (B) Heatmap showing two distinct groups of subjects identified based on robust clustering analysis of day 0 serologic and memory B-cell variables (see Methods) (C) Post-vaccination changes in plasmablast frequencies on day 7 for the low (1) and high (2) initial titer groups from B.

claim_13.claim: flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day 7 relative to vaccination (day 0), using diagonal linear discriminant analysis, showed that day 7 plasmablasts (ID87) and the overlapping CD20+CD27+CD38hi CD20− B cells (Plasmablasts) and CD20+IgD−CD27+ memory B cells (ID96) were predictive of day 70 maximum fold-change (MFC) and adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC) microneutralization assay titer responses.

sources.quote: In contrast, highly predictive models could be built using day 7 data for both adjMFC and MFC (Figures 5D).
Accordingly, plasmablasts (ID87) and the overlapping CD20+ subpopulation (ID96) were the dominant cellular contributors (Figure 5E) (Withers et al., 2007).

Figure 5. Predictive modeling of antibody response and identification of correlates (D) Prediction performance for MFC and adjMFC shown for models built using different number of top cell-populations (D) and genes (F) from day 7 (see Methods). (E) Day 7 predictive cell populations (see Results and Methods). The percentage of times (from 5000 random trials) a cell population is included in the model is shown. Median normalized weights of each population are shown on the right. The sign of the weight indicates the direction of correlation between the cell population and the titer endpoint.

claim_14.claim: microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day 1 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed that Interferon Signaling was positively associated with day 70 maximum fold-change (MFC) microneutralization assay titer responses.

sources.quote: While models built using either gene expression or cell populations from day 1 were not predictive, “Interferon Signaling” correlated robustly with MFC (Figure 5C).

Figure 5. Predictive modeling of antibody response and identification of correlates (C) Robust transcriptomic correlates from days 1 and 7 post-vaccination (shown as pathway enrichments) (see Methods). Percentage of times a pathway is enriched (p<0.05) is shown. Pathways significant for more than 80% of the trials for at least one time-point are shown.

claim_15.claim: microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day 7 relative to vaccination (day 0), using partial least square followed by linear discriminant analysis, showed gene-expression models predicted day 70 maximum fold-change (MFC) microneutralization assay titer responses using as few as 2 or 5 genes compared to chance prediction.

sources.quote: Consistent with previous findings (Nakaya et al., 2011), MFC could be predicted using as few as 2 or 5 genes, although more were required for adjMFC (Figure 5F).

Figure 5. Predictive modeling of antibody response and identification of correlates (D) Prediction performance for MFC and adjMFC shown for models built using different number of top cell-populations (D) and genes (F) from day 7 (see Methods).

claim_16.claim: microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day 7 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed ER stress, N-glycan biosynthesis, and cell cycle pathway genes were positively associated with plasmablast frequencies measured by flow cytometric analyses.

sources.quote: Notably, robustly correlated (Figure 5C) and predictive genes (Table S4) were enriched for “ER stress”, “N-glycan biosynthesis” and cell cycle pathways, whose gene members correlated strongly with plasmablast frequencies (see below).

claim_17.claim: microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day 0 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed genes associated with pattern recognition and Interferon signaling were positively associated with day 70 maximum fold-change (MFC) microneutralization assay titer responses, but less so with adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC).

sources.quote: Notably, genes associated with pattern recognition and Interferon signaling robustly correlated to MFC, but less so to adjMFC.
Figure 6. Day 0 predictors and correlates (A) Robust correlates between day 0 gene expression and response titers (see Figure 5C).

claim_18.claim: flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day 0 relative to vaccination (day 0), using diagonal linear discriminant analysis, showed cell-population frequencies alone predicted day 70 maximum fold-change (MFC) and adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC) microneutralization assay titer responses compared to models integrating pathway/transcript with cell-population data.

sources.quote: Notably, predictive models could be built by using cell populations alone (Figure 6B)—integrating pathway/transcript with cell population data performed substantially worse (best median AUC was 0.6 vs. 0.78 using cell populations alone). Thus, day 0 cell frequencies alone provided the essential information for prediction.
Figure 6. Day 0 predictors and correlates (B) Prediction performance using day 0 populations (as in Figure 5D).

claim_19.claim: flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day 0 relative to vaccination (day 0), using diagonal linear discriminant analysis, showed memory, naïve and transitional B cells, CD4 effector memory T cells, IFNα+ myeloid dendritic cells, and several activated T-cell populations were predictive of day 70 adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC) microneutralization assay titer responses compared to low responders.

sources.quote: Twelve cell populations were identified for adjMFC, including memory, naïve and transitional B cells, CD4 effector memory T cells, IFNα+ myeloid dendritic cells (mDC), and several activated T cell populations (Figure 6C; see Methods).
Figure 6. Day 0 predictors and correlates (C) Day 0 predictive cell populations analyzed as in Figure 5E.

claim_20.claim: flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day 0 relative to vaccination (day 0), using diagonal linear discriminant analysis, showed primarily T-cell subsets predicted day 70 maximum fold-change (MFC) microneutralization assay titer responses compared to the broader set of populations predictive for adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC).

sources.quote: Only some of these populations, primarily the T cell subsets, contributed to the prediction of MFC (Figure 6C).
Figure 6. Day 0 predictors and correlates (C) Day 0 predictive cell populations analyzed as in Figure 5E.

claim_21.claim: flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day -7, day 0, and day 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed all predictive B-cell populations except ID105 and some predictive CD4+ T-cell populations were remarkably stable within individuals over more than two months compared to their inter-subject variation.

sources.quote: Except for ID105 (CD86+IgD+ memory B cells), all of the B cell and some of the CD4+ T cell (including effector memory) predictive populations were remarkably stable within individuals over a period of more than two months (Figure 6D).

Figure 6. Day 0 predictors and correlates (D) Scatter plot of intra-subject stability (y) vs. inter-subject variance (x) (see Methods). Predictive populations from (C) are highlighted in blue (more stable populations) and yellow (less stable).

claim_22.claim: flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day 0 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed stable B-cell populations ID91, ID96, ID103, and ID108 were CD38+ and predicted adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC) microneutralization assay titer responses but not maximum fold-change (MFC).

sources.quote: These stable B-cell populations (ID91, 96, 103, 108) were all CD38+ and contributed to the prediction of adjMFC but not MFC.

claim_23.claim: flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day -7, day 0, day 1, day 7, and day 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed predictive cell populations remained able to separate high and low responders across timepoints compared to each other.

sources.quote: Examining the predictive cell populations' temporal profile further confirmed their stability and ability to separate the high and low responders (Figures 6E, 6F and S5).

Figure 6. Day 0 predictors and correlates (E-F) Temporal profiles of two stable predictive cell populations for high (orange) and low (green) responders (based on adjMFC). Missing data points correspond to samples with low viability.

claim_24.claim: flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day -7, day 0, day 7, and day 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed ID96 increased coherently on day 7 and returned to lower levels by day 70 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: This was true even for ID96, which increased coherently across subjects at day 7 post-vaccination and returned to lower levels by day 70.

claim_25.claim: flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day 0 relative to vaccination (day 0), using diagonal linear discriminant analysis, showed adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC) microneutralization assay titer responses could be robustly predicted using only the 56 most stable cell populations compared to chance prediction.

sources.quote: Even using a smaller k of 10 (versus 30 previously), adjMFC could be robustly predicted (median AUC=0.78; Figure 6G).
Figure 6. Day 0 predictors and correlates (G) Predictive performance for day 0 using only the temporally stable populations (those above the 80% mark in Figure 6D).

claim_26.claim: flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day 0 relative to vaccination (day 0), using diagonal linear discriminant analysis, showed omitting the stable cell populations preserved high predictive performance for maximum fold-change (MFC) but substantially reduced predictive performance for adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC) microneutralization assay titer responses compared to models retaining those stable populations.

sources.quote: However, if the stable populations above the 80% mark in Figure 6D were omitted instead, performance remained high for MFC (median AUC=0.83 for k=10), but dropped substantially for adjMFC (median AUC=0.56 for k=10).

claim_27.claim: flow cytometric analyses of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at baseline day -7, baseline day 0, and day 70 relative to vaccination (day 0), using diagonal linear discriminant analysis, showed models trained on day 0 cell-population data accurately predicted adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC) microneutralization assay titer responses using independent baseline measurements from day -7 and day 70 compared to chance prediction.

sources.quote: Highly accurate prediction could still be made for all k's, e.g., AUC=0.91 and AUC=0.86 for days -7 and 70 using k=10, respectively. Thus, the predictive signals were remarkably stable over time.

claim_28.claim: microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day 7 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed antigen secreting cell/B cell/plasmablast-specific genes including Ig chains, XBP1 and IRF4, and plasmablast-associated pathways including ER stress and N-glycan biosynthesis, were positively associated with the frequencies of predictive day 7 cell populations ID87 and ID96 measured by flow cytometric analyses.

sources.quote: As expected, the two predictive and coherently changing cell populations from day 7 (ID87 and ID96) were linked to known antigen secreting cell/B cell/plasmablast-specific genes, including Ig chains, XBP1 and IRF4, as well as plasmablast-associated pathways such as ER stress (Figures 7B and D).

These populations were also associated with N-glycan biosynthesis, consistent with the highly glycosylated state of immunoglobulins and the requirement for proper glycosylation for plasma cell development (Tulp et al., 1986).

Figure 7. Gene expression and pathway enrichment signatures of predictive cell populations Genes significantly correlated with predictive populations from (A) day 0 and (B) day 7. In (B), coherently changing genes from Figure 3 are highlighted by color denoting the clusters from Figure 3B. Analyses were performed separately for positively and negatively correlated genes (in red and blue scales respectively). Only genes significantly correlated with at least one population are shown (FDR<0.01). Pathway enrichment analyses of gene correlates of (C) day 0 and (D) day 7 predictive cell populations (from Figure 6C).

claim_29.claim: microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day 7 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed many plasmablast-correlated genes were the same genes that changed on day 7 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Many plasmablast-correlated genes were also ones that changed on day 7 (Figures 3B, C and 7B (marked in purple and orange)) and included genes found to be predictive of or correlated with response titers in previous studies (marked in blue; e.g., TNFRSF17).

Figure 7. Gene expression and pathway enrichment signatures of predictive cell populations Genes significantly correlated with predictive populations from (A) day 0 and (B) day 7. In (B), coherently changing genes from Figure 3 are highlighted by color denoting the clusters from Figure 3B. Analyses were performed separately for positively and negatively correlated genes (in red and blue scales respectively). Only genes significantly correlated with at least one population are shown (FDR<0.01).

claim_30.claim: microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day 0 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed several mitochondria-related pathways were positively associated with ID108 (CD38+ naïve B cells) and ID91 (CD38hi transitional B cells) measured by flow cytometric analyses.

sources.quote: Several mitochondria-related pathways were positively associated with ID108 (CD38+ naïve B cells) and ID91 (CD38hi transitional B cells), perhaps reflecting changes in bioenergetic states associated with B cell development and activation.

Pathway enrichment analyses of gene correlates of (C) day 0 and (D) day 7 predictive cell populations (from Figure 6C).

claim_31.claim: microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day 0 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed PRR signaling, TREM1 signaling, and interferon-related genes were positively associated with IL22+ and IL2+ CD4+ T cells and negatively associated with ID36 effector memory CD4+ T cells and ID50 perforin+ CD8+ cells measured by flow cytometric analyses.

sources.quote: Of note, several innate pathways (PRR signaling, TREM1 signaling, and interferon-related genes) were positively linked to IL22+ and IL2+ CD4+ T cells (ID25 and ID26), and negatively linked to ID36 and ID50.

In (B), coherently changing genes from Figure 3 are highlighted by color denoting the clusters from Figure 3B. Analyses were performed separately for positively and negatively correlated genes (in red and blue scales respectively). Only genes significantly correlated with at least one population are shown (FDR<0.01). Pathway enrichment analyses of gene correlates of (C) day 0 and (D) day 7 predictive cell populations (from Figure 6C).

claim_32.claim: microarrays analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals at day 0 and day 7 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed ID96 measured by flow cytometric analyses had largely distinct transcriptomic signatures at day 0 compared to day 7.

sources.quote: Interestingly, ID96, a day 0 predictive B-cell population that also coherently increased on day 7 (Figures 3D and 6F), showed largely distinct signatures on days 0 and 7 (Figures 7A-D), suggesting differences in the cell population defined by those markers, or distinct functional interactions with other cell populations post-vaccination.
